title: Review of ringswim at 256^2 (SIMD): fresh seed 11 gives a bounded swimming, dividing population with no band (143 persistent splits by the author's tracker, generation 14, 100 segments >= 3 BL vs 1 with mu=0); reticulate, and labkit's tracker finds 0 persistent splits (Supported)
summary: Looked at the README and strip_s10.png, then ran the claimed world.py at 256^2 on fresh seed 11 with labkit (rerun/seed11, T=20000) and the claim's celltrack.py, plus celltrack on a mu=0 twin of the same seed (world_mu0.py). The sheet shows walled cells from noise as round cells and crescents with wakes, 39 at the end (occupancy 0.18), moving, fusing and pinching to t=20000, and no domain-wrapping band. celltrack: 348 splits, 143 persistent, max generation 14, 229 merges (0.66 of splits), 100 track segments >= 3 BL and 20 >= 5 BL (best 10.9 BL); labkit: 14 long-lived tracks >= 1 BL, max 5.3 BL, 774 splits but 0 persistent at its 2000-t window. mu=0 twin: 1 segment >= 3 BL and 0 >= 5 BL, but still 136 persistent splits (generation 6) with 556 deaths and 1 merge, so the drive gives motility and makes the genealogy reticulate; division happens without it.

observations.S: rerun/seed11/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain
observations.I: rerun/seed11/sheet.png t=800-20000: discrete walled cells, 39 at the end, bounded occupancy 0.18
observations.M: data/celltrack_s11.log: 100 segments >= 3 BL, 20 >= 5 BL; mu=0 twin 1 and 0 (data/celltrack_mu0_s11.log)
observations.D: data/celltrack_s11.log: 143 persistent splits, max generation 14; rerun/seed11/sheet.png pinching cells

verdicts.limitation: Merges are 66% of splits (reticulate, caps confidence at medium), and labkit's own lineage window finds no persistent split, so D rests on the claim's overlap tracker. The drive is the per-body label average (nonlocal), as the claim says.
